turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until twenty to five, so let's not waste it. Who decided my son gets a zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." Your own procedure, section 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish anything, and the company's guide says the same, I have it printed in my bag. So either you have something else, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office when we're done.
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need more proof." I'm writing that down. Withdraw the zero today, or I'm in the principal's office at four forty-one.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." Are you calling my son a liar, Hale, or me? Choose your next sentence carefully, because it's going in my letter to the principal.

Then we're done negotiating and we're into procedure. Principal today, and if that goes nowhere, the board under section 42. Last chance to show me a single document with Owen's name and a date on it.
